questions.q: What is the minimum valid definition of a custom Apex exception?
options: `public class MyException extends Exception {}`
`public class MyException implements Exception {}`
`public interface MyException extends Exception {}`
`public class MyException extends DmlException {}`
questions.explain: A custom exception is created by extending the built-in Exception class; this minimal declaration is fully usable.

questions.q: How do you raise a custom exception instance so it propagates to a caller?
options: `raise new MyException('message');`
`MyException.fire('message');`
`throw new MyException('message');`
`return new MyException('message');`
questions.explain: The throw keyword, combined with new to construct the exception instance, raises it so it can be caught up the call stack.

questions.q: If `PaymentDeclinedException extends OrderException`, and calling code only writes `catch (OrderException oe)`, what happens when a `PaymentDeclinedException` is thrown?
options: It is not caught, because the catch block names a different class
It is caught by that block, since a catch on a type also matches its subclasses
It causes a compile error
It is caught but getMessage() returns null
questions.explain: Catch blocks match an exception's declared type or any of its supertypes, so catching OrderException also catches PaymentDeclinedException.

questions.q: What does `getCause()` return on a custom exception?
options: The line number where the exception was thrown
A list of all catch blocks that could handle it
The stack trace as a formatted string
The inner exception passed in when the custom exception was constructed, if any
questions.explain: When a custom exception is constructed with a message plus an inner exception, getCause() retrieves that wrapped inner exception.

questions.q: Can you directly `throw new DmlException('...')` the way you would throw a custom exception?
options: Yes, built-in exceptions can always be thrown manually
Only inside a trigger context
No — you can catch Apex's built-in exceptions, but you cannot throw them yourself; only custom exceptions you define are throwable in your own code
Only if allOrNone is set to false
questions.explain: Apex's built-in exception types can be caught but not thrown manually by your code; custom exceptions extending Exception are the ones you throw yourself.
